lines.say: What if the famous knight of faith
in this engraving was never a hero?
This is Knight,
Death and the Devil,
engraved by Albrecht Dürer in 1513.
For centuries,
the rider has been read
as a Christian soldier protected
by the armour of his faith.
Nietzsche even gave a print to Wagner
as a symbol of a brave future.
And the picture seems to agree.
The knight stares ahead while Death
and the Devil crowd beside his horse.
But look at his lance.
A fox tail hangs from its tip.
According to the writers Sten Karling and Ursula Meyer,
the work did not seek to glorify the knight.
In early Christian symbolism,
the fox stood for greed,
cunning and treachery.
And Dorothy Getlein saw his face
as resigned and downcast.
He isn't a hero of faith.
He's a resigned rider with Death as his companion.
So is he a saint in armour,
or a man who already gave up?
